summary: A 1934 Civilian Conservation Corps lookout on a 20-foot steel tower in the Sierra National Forest, staffed by volunteers since paid staffing ended in 1995.

facts.design: 14 x 14 ft C-3 cab with catwalk on a 20 ft H-braced steel tower

staffing.status: volunteer-staffed during fire season; paid staffing ended in 1995

access.note: Active volunteer lookout on Forest Service land. Do not park by the locked gate on the access road; the approach on foot is about two and a half miles. Neither source says whether the cab is open to visitors.

visit.trail_note: About two and a half miles of hiking to the tower from the access road off California Highway 49. Do not park by the locked gate.

events.note: Built by the CCC; both sources give 1934
Paid staffing discontinued because of budget cutbacks; volunteers have staffed the tower since
Volunteer Joe Knowles Jr. died on the evening of October 26 while on duty at the tower
Tower dedicated by the Sierra National Forest in Knowles's memory
Weather station installed during fiscal 2012; interior and exterior renovation reported in the 2011 and 2012 reports

evidence.supports: built by the CCC in 1934; remains in active service and staffed with volunteers
evidence.quote: Built by the CCC in 1934 on the Mariposa Ranger District of the Sierra National Forest, Miami Mountain Lookout remains in active service, and is now staffed with volunteers.

evidence.supports: 14 x 14 ft cab on a 20 ft steel tower
evidence.quote: The 14' x 14' C-3 cab with catwalk is mounted on a 20' H-braced steel tower.

evidence.supports: put into service by the Forest Service in 1934
evidence.quote: Miami Lookout was established and put into service by the Forest Service in 1934.

evidence.supports: 1933 visibility study identified the site as the only permanent lookout not used before
evidence.quote: The only permanent lookout on the Sierra National Forest identified in 1933 visibility study that had not previously been used as a lookout.

evidence.supports: paid staffing ended in 1995; volunteers since
evidence.quote: Miami Lookout is now staffed by local volunteers since cutbacks forced the discontinuance of paid staffing in 1995.

evidence.supports: fire season begins about May 15
evidence.quote: Miami is staffed during the declared fire season which begins about May 15th of each year.

evidence.supports: location about a mile west of Highway 49 and just north of Nipinnawasee
evidence.quote: Miami Mountain is located on the Mariposa, Madera County line one mile west of California State Highway 49.

evidence.supports: just north of Nipinnawasee
evidence.quote: about two miles off Highway 49 just north of Nipinnawasee

evidence.supports: do not park by the locked gate; vehicles may be towed
evidence.quote: Do not drive up and park by the locked gate, because your vehicle may be towed for blocking the access road.

evidence.supports: about two and a half miles to the tower on foot
evidence.quote: It is then a two and a half mile hike up to the tower

evidence.supports: full name Josiah Knowles, Jr. (Joe Knowles)
evidence.quote: my very best friend Josiah Knowles, Jr. (Joe Knowles)

evidence.supports: volunteer died on duty in 2006
evidence.quote: Joe passed away on the evening of October 26, 2006 while on duty at Miami Lookout and closing the tower for the evening.

evidence.supports: tower dedicated in 2009 in his memory
evidence.quote: On June 27, 2009, the Sierra National Forest dedicated the tower in his memory and name.

evidence.supports: 2011 interior and exterior renovation
evidence.quote: We are continuing the interior and external renovation of Miami Mountain Lookout.

evidence.supports: weather station installed in FY2012
evidence.quote: A weather station was also installed during FY2012.

evidence.supports: live cameras never repaired; no live view
evidence.quote: The live cams were never replaced or repaired, so there is no longer and live view from the tower for the public or fire departments.

evidence.supports: no updates on tower work since 2012; page last updated February 2017
evidence.quote: Since 2012, we have not been updated on any of the work that was performed on the tower

evidence.supports: page last updated February 25, 2017
evidence.quote: This page last updated on February 25, 2017.

evidence.supports: registered April 21, 1999
evidence.quote: April 21, 1999

evidence.supports: registered April 21, 1999 as Lookout No. 305
evidence.quote: Placed on the National Historic Lookout Register on 4/21/1999 as Lookout No. 305

evidence.supports: Bass Lake Ranger District (conflicts with NHLR's Mariposa Ranger District)
evidence.quote: Sierra National Forest, Bass Lake Ranger District

evidence.supports: elevation 4,285 ft (1,306 m)
elevation 4,327 ft (conflicts with NHLR)
evidence.quote: At an elevation of 4327 feet

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 4,285 ft (1,306 m); the volunteer page gives 4,327 ft. The record keeps the register figure and the story reports both.
The register places the lookout on the Mariposa Ranger District; the volunteer page says Bass Lake Ranger District. Not resolved.
The volunteer page gives the distance from Highway 49 as one mile in one passage and about two miles in another. The story reports both.

sources.title: Miami Mountain Fire Lookout, Sierra National Forest, Rich Camp

notes_for_editor: Both sources are dated or undated: the volunteer page was last updated February 2017 and the register page is undated. Current staffing and condition are unconfirmed. The brief's access 'unknown' is now 'restricted' based on the locked-gate note; check with the Sierra National Forest before changing it. The record's values for county, year built and registration all check out; no corrections proposed.
